extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators of CCR units; facility environmental compliance managers; consulting engineers; state and EPA permitting authorities
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and performance criteria for closing, retrofitting, and conducting post-closure care of Coal Combustion Residuals (CCR) units, including timelines, engineering/design standards, monitoring and documentation, notifications, deed notations, and recordkeeping obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure by removal — completion condition
rubrics_metrics.description: Closure by removal is complete when CCR has been removed; any areas affected by releases from the CCR unit have been removed or decontaminated; and groundwater monitoring concentrations of the constituents listed in appendix IV to this part do not exceed groundwater protection standards established pursuant to §257.95(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removal and decontamination activities include removing all CCR from the unit, CCR mixed with soils, and CCR included in berms, liners or other unit structures, and removing or decontaminating all areas affected by releases from the CCR unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure by removal — documentation and verification (active life completion)
rubrics_metrics.description: When electing closure by removal completed during the active life of the CCR unit, owner/operator must (i) complete removal and decontamination; (ii) document that standards in paragraph (c) have been met via groundwater monitoring results showing no constituents detected at statistically significant levels above groundwater protection standards either for two consecutive monitoring events or for three years in accordance with §257.98(c); and (iii) obtain the completion of closure certification or approval required by paragraph (f)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation must consist of groundwater monitoring results that meet the two-consecutive-event or three-year criteria; closure certification must be by a qualified professional engineer or Participating State Director or EPA (as applicable). Timeframes for these actions are specified in paragraph (f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure by removal with post-closure groundwater corrective action (hybrid completion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner/operator may remove and decontaminate all CCR except complete groundwater corrective action during post-closure care; must document removal/decontamination, begin implementation of remedy required by §257.97 so components are constructed/operating as intended (unless both applicable requirements §§257.96–257.98 met and active life could not be extended), complete groundwater corrective action as a post-closure requirement per §257.104(g), amend closure and post-closure plans, obtain closure certification/approval, and record deed notation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actions and certifications must occur within the timeframes in paragraph (f); remedy implementation must be documented unless delay is justified and documented; deed notation and plan amendments are required as part of closeout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure performance standard when leaving CCR in place — general
rubrics_metrics.description: When leaving CCR in place, owner/operator must ensure closure is conducted so that, at a minimum, the CCR unit will: (i) control, minimize or eliminate, to the maximum extent feasible, post-closure infiltration of liquids into the waste and releases of CCR, leachate, or contaminated run-off to ground/surface waters or atmosphere; (ii) preclude probability of future impoundment of water, sediment, or slurry; (iii) include measures providing for major slope stability to prevent sloughing or movement of the final cover during closure and post-closure care; (iv) minimize need for further maintenance; and (v) be completed in the shortest time consistent with recognized and generally accepted good engineering practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a performance-based standard — designs and actions must achieve these outcomes and be documented in the written closure plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drainage and stabilization prior to final cover
rubrics_metrics.description: Before installing the final cover when leaving CCR in place, free liquids must be eliminated by removing liquid wastes or solidifying remaining wastes and residues, and remaining wastes must be stabilized sufficient to support the final cover system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are prerequisite engineering activities to assure final cover performance and slope stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final cover system — prescriptive design criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: If closed by leaving CCR in place, the final cover system must be designed and constructed to minimize infiltration and erosion and, at minimum, meet criteria: (A) permeability ≤ permeability of bottom liner system or natural subsoils, or ≤ 1×10^-5 cm/sec, whichever is less; (B) infiltration minimized by an infiltration layer with minimum 18 inches of earthen material; (C) erosion minimized by an erosion layer with minimum 6 inches of earthen material capable of sustaining native plant growth; (D) design accommodates settling and subsidence to minimize disruption of integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design of the final cover system must be included in the written closure plan required by paragraph (b). These are minimum prescriptive measures; owners/operators may exceed them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final cover system — alternative design option and equivalency
rubrics_metrics.description: An owner/operator may select an alternative final cover system provided it is designed and constructed to meet equivalency criteria: (A) infiltration layer must achieve equivalent reduction in infiltration as specified in (i)(A) and (B); (B) erosion layer must provide equivalent protection from wind/water erosion as specified in (i)(C); (C) design must accommodate settling and subsidence to minimize disruption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative designs must demonstrate equivalent performance and must be included in the written closure plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final cover certification or approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner/operator must obtain a written certification from a qualified professional engineer or approval from the Participating State Director or approval from EPA (as permitting authority) that the design of the final cover system meets the requirements of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification/approval is required before implementation and must be placed in the facility's operating record as specified elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiation of closure — mandatory start timeframes
rubrics_metrics.description: Closure must commence no later than the applicable timeframes: (1) no later than 30 days after the date the CCR unit either receives the known final receipt of waste (CCR or non-CCR) or removes the known final volume of CCR for beneficial use; or (2) except as provided in (2)(ii), commence closure within two years of last receipt or last removal for beneficial use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commencement of closure is defined as cessation of placing waste plus any of: steps to implement the written closure plan, submitted completed permit application, or steps to comply with prerequisite state/agency standards. Specific exceptions and extension procedures exist (see following criteria).

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiation of closure — idle-unit extensions (additional two years)
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner/operator may secure an additional two years to initiate closure of an idle unit if they provide written documentation that the CCR unit will continue to accept wastes or will start removing CCR for beneficial use; documentation must include (A) info documenting remaining storage/disposal capacity or ability to have CCR removed for beneficial use; and (B) info demonstrating reasonable likelihood CCR unit will resume receiving wastes or CCR can be removed for beneficial use, including a best estimate of timing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of supporting situations include alternating use of multiple CCR units, temporarily idled boilers likely to resume, CCR diverted to beneficial uses but could resume use, or temporary absence of non-CCR waste streams with reasonable likelihood of future receipt. Each completed demonstration must be placed in the operating record prior to the end of any two-year period if more than one extension is sought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiation of closure — certification for extension requests
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain additional time extension(s) to initiate closure beyond two years, owner/operator must include a signed statement certifying under penalty of law that the submitted demonstration and attached documents are true, accurate, and complete and that the signer has personally examined and is familiar with the information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This signed certification carries penalty of law (fine/imprisonment) for false submissions and must be included with the extension demonstration in the operating record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to initiation timeframes
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard initiation timeframes do not apply to specified categories of owners/operators, including (reserved) and owners/operators closing as required by §257.101 for certain existing or new CCR surface impoundments and CCR landfills (see §257.101 references).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check §257.101 for the specific categories exempted from the general initiation timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion of closure — standard deadlines by unit type
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in (f)(2), owner/operator must complete closure: (i) for existing/new CCR landfills and any lateral expansion, within 6 months of commencing closure activities; (ii) for existing/new CCR surface impoundments and lateral expansions, within 5 years of commencing closure activities; (iii) for CCR management units, within 5 years of commencing closure activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are baseline completion deadlines; extensions are available under specified circumstances (next entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion of closure — extensions for infeasible completion and supporting factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Timeframes for completing closure may be extended if owner/operator demonstrates it was not feasible to complete within required timeframes due to factors beyond facility's control. The demonstration must include a narrative discussion providing basis for additional time and be placed in operating record prior to the end of any two-year period if more than one extension is sought. Factors that may support the demonstration include unusual climate/weather, time to dewater unit, surrounding geology/terrain affecting material needs, and time/delays to coordinate and obtain approvals/permits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each extension request must substantiate factual circumstances demonstrating need.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion of closure — maximum allowable time extension rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximum extensions differ by unit type and size: (A) CCR surface impoundments ≤ 40 acres may extend closure by no longer than 2 years; (B) surface impoundments > 40 acres may extend multiple times in two-year increments but no more than five two-year extensions total; (C) CCR landfills may extend multiple times in one-year increments but no more than two one-year extensions total, except (D) landfills that intersect groundwater may use the impoundment extension rules if documented; (E)-(F) CCR management units follow the same ≤40 acre and >40 acre rules as impoundments with two-year increments up to five two-year extensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each extension sought, the owner/operator must substantiate factual circumstances demonstrating need; documentation requirements and placement in operating record apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion of closure — certification for extension requests
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain additional time extension(s) beyond the standard times, owner/operator must include a signed certification under penalty of law that they have examined and are familiar with the submitted information and that it is true, accurate and complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the same legal attestation requirement as for initiation extensions and must be placed in the operating record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion of closure — final certification/approval upon completion
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon completion, the owner/operator must obtain a certification from a qualified professional engineer or approval from the Participating State Director or EPA verifying that closure has been completed in accordance with the closure plan and the requirements of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification/approval must be obtained and the documentation placed in the operating record per recordkeeping rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of intent to close — timing and contents
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than the date the owner/operator initiates closure, they must prepare a notification of intent to close the CCR unit. The notification must include the certification by a qualified professional engineer or the Participating State Director/EPA approval for the design of the final cover system, if applicable. The notification is completed when placed in the facility's operating record as required by §257.105(i)(7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare and place the notification in the operating record contemporaneously with initiation actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of completion of closure — timing and contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 days of completion of closure, the owner/operator must prepare a notification of closure of the CCR unit that includes the required certification/approval per §257.102(f)(3). The notification is complete when placed in the operating record as required by §257.105(i)(8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely prepare and place the completion notification may violate operating record and notification requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deed notations — recording and required content
rubrics_metrics.description: Following closure, owner/operator must record a notation on the deed (or other instrument normally examined during title search) that in perpetuity notifies any potential purchaser that (i) the land has been used as a CCR unit; and (ii) its use is restricted under the post-closure care requirements in §257.104(d)(1)(iii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within 30 days of recording the notation, the owner/operator must prepare a notification stating the notation has been recorded and place it in the operating record per §257.105(i)(9). Owners/operators closing by removal under §257.102(c)(1) are not subject to these deed notation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure recordkeeping, notification, and internet requirements cross-reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner/operator must comply with closure recordkeeping requirements in §257.105(i), closure notification requirements in §257.106(i), and closure internet requirements in §257.107(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a cross-reference directing where to find specific recordkeeping, notification, and web posting requirements associated with closure activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria to retrofit an existing CCR surface impoundment — prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: To retrofit an existing CCR surface impoundment, the owner/operator must (i) first remove all CCR, including any contaminated soils and sediments from the CCR unit; and (ii) comply with requirements in §257.72. A CCR surface impoundment undergoing a retrofit remains subject to all other requirements of this subpart, including requirement to conduct any necessary corrective action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retrofitting does not suspend other regulatory obligations; contaminated soils and sediments must be removed before retrofit work proceeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written retrofit plan — required content
rubrics_metrics.description: The written retrofit plan must describe steps necessary to retrofit consistent with recognized and generally accepted good engineering practices and must include at minimum: (A) narrative description of specific measures to retrofit the CCR unit; (B) description of procedures to remove all CCR and contaminated soils/sediments; (C) estimate of maximum amount of CCR to be removed as part of retrofit; (D) estimate of largest area of CCR unit affected by retrofit; (E) schedule for completing activities necessary to satisfy retrofit criteria, including estimated year in which retrofit activities will be completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plan must be prepared in accordance with the timing provisions (next entries) and be placed in the operating record with required certifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written retrofit plan — timing for initial plan and completion of plan in operating record
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than 60 days prior to initiating retrofit activities, the owner/operator must prepare an initial written retrofit plan. Initiation of retrofit activities is defined similarly to initiation of closure. The owner/operator has completed the written retrofit plan when the plan, including required certification, has been placed in the facility's operating record as required by §257.105(j)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare and certify the retrofit plan and place it in the operating record before commencing physical retrofit activities (or within the specified timing when retrofit initiation conditions are met).

rubrics_metrics.name: Written retrofit plan — amendment requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner/operator may amend the initial or any subsequent retrofit plan at any time. The plan must be amended whenever (1) there is a change in operation substantially affecting the plan, or (2) before or after retrofit activities, unanticipated events necessitate a revision. Amend at least 60 days prior to a planned change or no later than 60 days after an unanticipated event; if revised after retrofit activities have commenced, amend no later than 30 days following the triggering event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments must be documented, certified, and placed in the operating record per certification/approval requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retrofit certification/approval (plan and completion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner/operator must obtain a written certification from a qualified professional engineer or approval from the Participating State Director or EPA that the activities outlined in the written retrofit plan, including any amendment, meet requirements of this section. Upon completion of retrofit, the owner/operator must obtain a written certification/approval verifying retrofit activities have been completed in accordance with the plan and requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certifications/approvals must be placed in the operating record. Retrofit remains subject to corrective action and other subpart requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline for completion of retrofit activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Any CCR surface impoundment being retrofitted must complete all retrofit activities within the same time frames and procedures specified for closure of a CCR surface impoundment in §257.102(f) or, where applicable, §257.103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use closure completion timelines and extension rules for retrofits; extension/substantiation/certification rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retrofit notifications and completion notices
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than the date owner/operator initiates the retrofit they must prepare a notification of intent to retrofit and place it in the operating record per §257.105(j)(5). Within 30 days of completing retrofit activities, the owner/operator must prepare a notification of completion including required certification/approval and place it in the operating record per §257.105(j)(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notifications are complete when placed in the operating record; certifications must be included with completion notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cease retrofit and initiate closure option
rubrics_metrics.description: At any time after initiation of a CCR unit retrofit, the owner/operator may cease the retrofit and initiate closure of the CCR unit in accordance with the requirements of §257.102.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Switching from retrofit to closure triggers the closure initiation, completion, and notification requirements applicable under §257.102.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retrofit recordkeeping, notification, and internet requirements cross-reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner/operator must comply with retrofit recordkeeping requirements in §257.105(j), retrofit notification requirements in §257.106(j), and retrofit internet requirements in §257.107(j).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These cross-references identify where retrofit-specific recordkeeping and public/internet posting obligations are specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-closure care applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: §257.104 applies to owners/operators of CCR units subject to closure criteria under §257.102, except owners/operators that elect to close by removing CCR as provided by §257.102(c)(1) are not subject to the post-closure care criteria under this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether post-closure obligations apply based on chosen closure method (leaving CCR in place triggers post-closure care; removal may exempt the unit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-closure care duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided elsewhere, owner/operator must conduct post-closure care for 30 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions exist (e.g., units closed under §257.102(c)(2) complete groundwater corrective action per §257.98(c) — consult the rule for details).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines to prepare initial written post-closure plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Deadlines differ by unit type: (i) existing CCR landfills and existing CCR surface impoundments: no later than October 17, 2016; (ii) new CCR landfills, new CCR surface impoundments, and any lateral expansion: no later than date of initial receipt of CCR; (iii) CCR management units: no later than November 8, 2028. The owner/operator has completed the written post-closure plan when the plan, including required certification, has been placed in the operating record as required by §257.105(i)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to the specified calendar dates for existing units and to the receipt date for new units; include required certifications and place in operating record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of a deed notation after corrective action and post-closure completion
rubrics_metrics.description: An owner/operator of a CCR unit closed pursuant to §§257.102(c)(2) and 257.104 may remove the deed notation specified in §257.102(i) upon: (1) completion of groundwater corrective action demonstrating affected areas do not exceed groundwater protection standards established pursuant to §257.95(h) for constituents listed in appendix IV; and (2) completion of the notification of completion of post-closure care period required by paragraph (e) of §257.104.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removal of the deed notation requires both demonstrated attainment of groundwater protection standards and completion of required post-closure notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operating record — general maintenance and dating requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each owner/operator must date and maintain files of all information required by this subpart in a written operating record at their facility, and each file must indicate the date the file was placed in the operating record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operating record is the primary repository for demonstrations, notifications, plans, certifications, and other required documents; timely placement is frequently the metric of compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document retention period
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless specified otherwise, each file must be retained for at least five years following the date of each occurrence, measurement, maintenance, corrective action, report, record, or study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some documents have special retention rules that extend beyond five years (see design criteria list).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping for multiple CCR units
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators with more than one CCR unit may comply with recordkeeping in one system provided the system identifies each file by the name of each CCR unit. Files may be maintained on microfilm, computer, disks, storage systems, magnetic tape, or microfiche.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single system is allowed if files are clearly organized by unit name to demonstrate unit-specific compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: State Director / Tribal authority notification of requested demonstrations/documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner/operator must submit to the State Director and/or appropriate Tribal authority any demonstration or documentation required by this subpart if requested, when such information is not otherwise available on the owner/operator's CCR website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to provide requested materials to regulators/tribal authorities; maintain public web posting to reduce ad hoc document requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Location restrictions demonstration placement and retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner/operator must place demonstrations documenting compliance with §§257.60(a), 257.61(a), 257.62(a), 257.63(a), and 257.64(a) in the facility's operating record as they become available; each such demonstration must be maintained for five years after completion of closure by removal under §257.102(c) or until completion of post-closure care under §257.104(e) or (g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These specific location restriction demonstrations have extended retention tied to closure/post-closure milestones rather than the default five-year rule alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design criteria and related documentation required in operating record
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner/operator must place specified design and construction certifications, liner documentation, permanent marker documentation, hazard classification assessments, emergency action plans and activations, construction history, structural stability and safety factor assessments, corrective measures documentation, design/construction plans and revisions, applications and supplemental materials, alternative liner/alternative source demonstrations and related decisions, facility evaluation reports (parts 1 & 2), and other enumerated documents in the operating record as they become available. Many of these documents must be maintained for five years after completion of closure by removal or until completion of post-closure care irrespective of the default five-year retention rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule enumerates (f)(1) through (f)(26) specific items and special retention rules for each. Owners/operators should consult the specific subparagraphs to identify retention periods and required content for each document type.
